root = Stack([TextExplanation, Diagram])

TextExplanation = Text(
"Geometric Meaning of Vector Dot Product:\n"
"The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. "
"Mathematically, for vectors A and B, the dot product A·B = |A||B|cos(θ), where θ is the angle between them.\n\n"
"Key points:\n"
"1. Projection: The dot product equals the length of one vector times the projection of the other onto it.\n"
"2. Orthogonal Vectors: If A·B = 0, vectors are perpendicular (θ = 90°), meaning no projection.\n"
"3. Negative Projection: If A·B < 0, the angle θ is greater than 90°, indicating the projection is opposite in direction."
)

Diagram = Graphic("DotProductDiagram", [
  // Draw vector A from origin
  path("M 50 100 L 150 50"), // vector A
  text(155, 45, "A"),
  // Draw vector B at angle θ < 90°
  path("M 50 100 L 120 130"), // vector B
  text(125, 135, "B"),
  // Draw projection of B onto A
  path("M 120 130 L 120 90 L 150 90"), // projection line vertical and horizontal to A
  path("M 120 90 L 150 90"), // projection on A line
  text(130, 85, "Projection of B on A"),
  // Angle θ mark
  path("M 50 100 L 70 90 L 80 100"),
  text(70, 80, "θ"),
  // Orthogonal vectors example
  path("M 250 100 L 350 100"), // vector A'
  text(355, 100, "A'"),
  path("M 250 100 L 250 30"), // vector B' orthogonal to A'
  text(255, 30, "B'"),
  // Negative projection example
  path("M 400 100 L 480 50"), // vector A''
  text(485, 45, "A''"),
  path("M 400 100 L 350 130"), // vector B'' with angle > 90°
  text(345, 135, "B''"),
  // Projection line for negative projection
  path("M 350 130 L 400 130 L 400 100"),
  text(375, 135, "Negative Projection")
])
